title: THE AIR (PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF POLLUTION) ACT, 1981
long_title: An Act to provide for the prevention, control and abatement of air pollution, for the establishment, with a view to carrying out the aforesaid purposes, of Boards, for conferring on and assigning to such Boards powers and functions relating thereto and for matters connected therewith.

sections.text: (1) This Act may be called the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

Defines key terms including "air pollutant", "air pollution", "approved appliance", "approved fuel", "automobile", "Board", "Central Board", "chimney", "control equipment", "emission", "industrial plant", "member", "occupier", "prescribed", "State Board", "State Government", and other related expressions.

chapters.chapter_title: CENTRAL AND STATE BOARDS FOR THE PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF AIR POLLUTION

sections.text: The Central Pollution Control Board constituted under section 3 of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 shall, without prejudice to the exercise and performance of its powers and functions under that Act, exercise the powers and perform the functions of the Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution under this Act.

sections.section_title: State Pollution Control Boards constituted under section 4 of Act 6 of 1974 to be State Boards under this Act
sections.text: In any State in which the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 is in force and the State Government has constituted a State Pollution Control Board under section 4 of that Act, such State Board shall be deemed to be the State Board for the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution constituted under section 5 of this Act, and shall exercise the powers and perform the functions of a State Board under this Act.

Where the Water Act is not in force or no State Board has been constituted under that Act, the State Government shall constitute a State Board for the Prevention and Control of Air Pollution consisting of a Chairman and other members as prescribed, representing various interests and Government departments.

sections.section_title: Central Board to exercise the powers and perform the functions of a State Board in the Union territories
sections.text: In relation to a Union territory, the Central Board shall exercise the powers and perform the functions of a State Board under this Act for that Union territory.

sections.section_title: Terms and conditions of service of members
sections.text: Provides for the term of office, conditions of service, and other terms applicable to the members of a State Board, including the Chairman.

Specifies the grounds on which a person shall be disqualified for being nominated or continuing as a member of a State Board (insolvency, unsound mind, conviction involving moral turpitude, conflict of interest, etc.).
Provides for the circumstances in which the seat of a member of a State Board becomes vacant, and the procedure for filling casual vacancies.

A Board shall meet at such times and places and observe such rules of procedure in regard to the transaction of business at its meetings as may be prescribed; the Chairman or any other member chosen by those present shall preside.

A Board may constitute as many committees consisting wholly of members or wholly of other persons or partly of members and partly of other persons as it thinks fit for the purpose of discharging its duties.

sections.section_title: Temporary association of persons with Board for particular purpose
sections.text: A Board may associate with itself in such manner and for such purposes as may be prescribed any person whose assistance or advice it may desire to obtain in performing any of its functions under this Act.

sections.section_title: Vacancy in Board not to invalidate acts or proceedings
sections.text: No act or proceeding of a Board or any committee thereof shall be called in question on the ground merely of the existence of any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution of, the Board or such committee.

sections.section_title: Member-secretary and officers and other employees of State Boards
sections.text: The State Government shall appoint a full-time member-secretary of the State Board possessing prescribed qualifications, and the Board may appoint such other officers and employees as it considers necessary; their conditions of service shall be as prescribed.
A Board may, by general or special order, delegate to the Chairman or any other officer of the Board such of its powers and functions under this Act as it may deem necessary.

The main functions of the Central Board shall be to improve the quality of air and to prevent, control or abate air pollution in the country. Without prejudice to generality, it shall advise the Central Government, plan and execute a nation-wide programme, coordinate activities of State Boards, provide technical assistance and guidance, collect and disseminate information, organise training, lay down standards, and perform other prescribed functions.

The functions of a State Board shall be to plan a comprehensive programme for prevention, control or abatement of air pollution, advise the State Government, collect and disseminate information, collaborate with the Central Board, inspect air pollution control areas, lay down emission standards, and perform other functions as prescribed or as directed by the Central Board or State Government.

(1) In the performance of its functions under this Act, the Central Board shall be bound by such directions in writing as the Central Government may give to it. (2) Every State Board shall be bound by such directions as the Central Board or the State Government may give to it.

chapters.chapter_title: PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF AIR POLLUTION

sections.section_title: Power to declare air pollution control areas
sections.text: The State Government may, after consultation with the State Board, by notification in the Official Gazette, declare any area or areas within the State as air pollution control area or areas for the purposes of this Act, and may alter such areas.

sections.section_title: Power to give instructions for ensuring standards for emission from automobiles
sections.text: With a view to ensuring that the standards for emission of air pollutants from automobiles laid down by the State Board under clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 17 are complied with, the State Government shall, in consultation with the State Board, give such instructions as may be deemed necessary to the concerned authority in charge of registration of motor vehicles under the Motor Vehicles Act.

sections.section_title: Restrictions on use of certain industrial plants
sections.text: No person shall, without the previous consent of the State Board, establish or operate any industrial plant in an air pollution control area. Application for consent shall be made in the prescribed form and accompanied by the prescribed fees. The Board may grant consent subject to conditions or refuse consent after giving opportunity of being heard.
The Central Government may issue guidelines for the grant, refusal or cancellation of consent under section 21, and for other matters connected with the prevention and control of air pollution.

sections.section_title: Persons carrying on industry, etc., not to allow emission of air pollutants in excess of the standard laid down by State Board
sections.text: No person operating any industrial plant in any air pollution control area shall discharge or cause or permit to be discharged the emission of any air pollutant in excess of the standards laid down by the State Board under clause (g) of sub-section (1) of section 17.

sections.section_title: Power of Board to make application to court for restraining persons from causing air pollution
sections.text: Where it is apprehended that emission of any air pollutant is likely to occur or is occurring in excess of standards, the Board may make an application to a court for restraining such person from emitting the pollutant, and the court may issue such order as it deems fit.

sections.section_title: Furnishing of information to State Board and other agencies in certain cases
sections.text: Where in any area the emission of any air pollutant into the atmosphere in excess of the standards occurs or is apprehended to occur due to accident or other unforeseen act or event, the person in charge of the premises shall forthwith intimate the fact of such occurrence or apprehension to the State Board and such authorities as may be prescribed.

Any person empowered by a State Board in this behalf shall have a right to enter any place for the purpose of examining any control equipment, industrial plant, record, register or document, or for conducting a search, and may seize any such equipment, plant or document if he has reason to believe that an offence under this Act has been committed.

For the purposes of carrying out the functions entrusted to it, the State Board or any officer empowered by it may call for any information including information regarding the types of air pollutants emitted and the level of emission of such pollutants from any person or occupier.

sections.section_title: Power to take samples of air or emission and procedure to be followed in connection therewith
sections.text: A State Board or any officer empowered by it may take samples of air or emission from any chimney, flue or duct or any other outlet for analysis; the procedure for taking samples, sealing, and analysis shall be as prescribed.

sections.section_title: Reports of the result of analysis on samples taken under section 26
sections.text: Where a sample has been taken under section 26, the result of the analysis shall be reported in the prescribed form, and a copy of the report shall be sent to the occupier or person in charge of the place from which the sample was taken.

The State Government may, by notification, establish one or more State Air Laboratories, or declare any laboratory or institute as a State Air Laboratory, for carrying out analysis of samples of air or emission.
The State Government may appoint persons having the prescribed qualifications to be Government analysts for the purpose of analysis of samples of air or emission.
Any document purporting to be a report signed by a Government analyst or a State Air Laboratory may be used as evidence of the facts stated therein in any proceeding under this Act.
Any person aggrieved by an order made by the State Board under this Act may prefer an appeal to such authority as the State Government may constitute, within the prescribed time and manner.

Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, a Board may, in the exercise of its powers and performance of its functions under this Act, issue any directions in writing to any person, officer or authority, and such person, officer or authority shall be bound to comply with such directions. Directions may include closure, prohibition or regulation of any industry, operation or process, or stoppage of supply of electricity, water or any other service.

Any person aggrieved by an order or decision of the Appellate Authority under section 31 or of the State Government or any other authority under this Act may file an appeal to the National Green Tribunal established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
The Central Government may, after due appropriation made by Parliament by law in this behalf, make such contribution to a State Board as it may think fit for the purpose of this Act.

Every State Board shall have its own fund, and all sums which may from time to time be paid to it by the Central Government or State Government and all other receipts shall be carried to the fund and all payments shall be made therefrom.

A Board may, with the consent of, or in accordance with the terms of any general or special authority given by, the Central Government or State Government, borrow money from any source for the purpose of this Act.

Every Board shall, during each financial year, prepare in such form and at such time as may be prescribed a budget in respect of the financial year next ensuing showing the estimated receipts and expenditure, and forward copies to the Central Government or State Government as the case may be.

Every Board shall, during each financial year, prepare an annual report giving a true and full account of its activities during the previous financial year and forward copies to the Central Government or State Government, which shall cause the report to be laid before Parliament or the State Legislature.

Every Board shall maintain proper accounts and other relevant records and prepare an annual statement of accounts in such form as may be prescribed; the accounts shall be audited by an auditor appointed by the Central Government or State Government, and the audited accounts shall be forwarded to the appropriate Government for being laid before the legislature.

sections.section_title: Failure to comply with the provisions of section 21 or section 22 or with the directions issued under section 31A
sections.text: Whoever fails to comply with the provisions of section 21 or section 22 or directions issued under section 31A shall be liable to penalty as provided under the Act (as amended, including provisions for adjudication and Environmental Protection Fund).

Whoever destroys, pulls down, removes, injures or defaces any pillar, post or stake fixed in the ground or any notice or other matter put up by a Board, or obstructs any person acting under the orders of a Board, or damages any works executed by a Board, shall be punishable as provided.

sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention by Government Department
sections.text: Where an offence under this Act has been committed by any Department of Government, the Head of the Department shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly, unless he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence to prevent it.

sections.section_title: Penalty for contravention of certain provisions of this Act
sections.text: Whoever contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or any order or direction issued thereunder for which no penalty has been elsewhere provided shall be punishable with the penalty provided under the Act.
The Central Government or State Government may appoint adjudicating officers for holding inquiries and imposing penalties under this Act; such officers shall have the powers of a civil court.
Any person aggrieved by an order of an adjudicating officer may prefer an appeal to the National Green Tribunal or such other authority as may be prescribed.

sections.section_title: Penalty amount to be credited to Environmental Protection Fund
sections.text: The amount of penalty imposed under this Act shall be credited to the Environmental Protection Fund constituted under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

sections.section_title: Offences for failure to comply with provisions of section 21 and for failure to pay penalty
sections.text: Failure to comply with the provisions of section 21 or failure to pay the penalty imposed under this Act shall constitute an offence punishable as provided.

sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
sections.text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government or any officer of Government or any member or officer or employee of a Board for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done under this Act or the rules made thereunder.

No court shall take cognizance of any offence under this Act except on a complaint made by a Board or any officer authorised in this behalf by it, or by any person who has given notice of not less than sixty days of the alleged offence to the Board.

sections.section_title: Members, officers and employees of Board to be public servants
sections.text: All members, officers and employees of a Board when acting or purporting to act in pursuance of any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

The Central Board shall, in relation to its functions under this Act, furnish to the Central Government such reports, returns, statistics, accounts and other information as that Government may from time to time require; a State Board shall furnish similar information to the State Government and to the Central Board.

No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which a Board is empowered by or under this Act to deal with, and no injunction shall be granted by any court in respect of any action taken or to be taken by a Board in pursuance of any power conferred by or under this Act.

sections.section_title: Power of State Government to supersede State Board
sections.text: If at any time the State Government is of opinion that a State Board has persistently made default in the performance of the functions imposed on it by or under this Act, or has exceeded or abused its powers, the State Government may, by notification, supersede the Board for such period as may be specified and appoint a person or persons to exercise the powers and perform the functions of the Board during the period of supersession.

sections.section_title: Special provision in the case of supersession of the Central Board or the State Boards constituted under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
sections.text: Where the Central Board or any State Board constituted under the Water Act is superseded under that Act, such Board shall be deemed to have been superseded under this Act also, and the provisions of this Act relating to supersession shall apply accordingly.

sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to supersede the Central Board or the State Boards constituted under the Water Act for violation of directions
sections.text: If the Central Government is of opinion that the Central Board or any State Board has defaulted in complying with any directions given by it, it may supersede such Board in the manner provided.
The Central Government may, by notification, amend the Schedule by adding or omitting any industry, and on such notification the Schedule shall be deemed to be amended accordingly.
Every State Board shall maintain a register containing such particulars of the persons to whom consent is granted under section 21 as may be prescribed, and the register shall be open to inspection.

Save as otherwise provided by or under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and subject to the provisions of section 53, the provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any enactment other than this Act.

The Central Government may, by notification, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act in relation to the Central Board, and the State Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act in relation to the State Board; rules may cover all procedural and substantive matters required to be prescribed.

sections.section_title: Rules to be laid before Parliament or State Legislature
sections.text: Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament or the State Legislature, as the case may be, and shall be subject to modification or annulment as provided.

schedule.title: THE SCHEDULE
schedule.description: List of industries in respect of which certain provisions of the Act (particularly consent requirements under section 21 as originally enacted) applied; the Schedule has been amended from time to time and certain industry-specific restrictions have been modified by subsequent amendments.
